brief: US equities faded sharply intraday on Nov 19, 2026. A roughly 400bp slide into the close left the S&P down 202bps at 7,175 (NDX -221bps to 26,517, Dow -219bps to 49,097, R2K -202bps to 2,659), even as the Nasdaq 100 stayed up 5% YTD. No single catalyst was identified. Some cited an AMD short report as a sentiment drag. Asset managers and hedge funds net sold macro products while net buying pockets of consumer and financials, and no sector screened materially for sale. Poor liquidity, with S&P top-of-book averaging just $4mm, exacerbated the price action. The day's largest-ever IPO debuted with strong demand, and options vol rallied hard on the post-open sell-off. VIX closed above 28, the term structure inverted more than 4 vol points over the front future, the most since April 2025, and tomorrow's straddle priced a 1.43% move. Desks saw no appetite to fade the selloff, with flows running to put and put-spread buying plus a 20,000-lot VIX December put tree. Dealers are estimated near max short vega into Friday's expiry, which the desk says needs to unwind before the market can stabilize.
